# Glossary

The words that brig and `brig ui` use. `brig help TOPIC` prints the same texts in a terminal, and `brig ui` shows them as hints and in its help pane; `brig help topics` lists them.

## Concepts

### Activity<a id="activity"></a>

Everything brig did, whether brig ui ran it or you did in a terminal, with the same steps the terminal shows.

In `brig ui`: `/activity`.

The whole story: [`how-to/scripting.md`](../how-to/scripting.md#the-activity-log).

In a terminal: `brig help activity`.

### Audit mode<a id="audit-mode"></a>

A rule in audit mode lets requests pass and logs what enforcing it would deny.

Also called: enforce, enforcement.

See also: [Verdict](#verdict), [Fence 1, the sandbox policy](#fence-1), [Audit trail](#audit-trail).

```sh
brig policy allow dev webapp HOST --binary PATH --audit
```

The whole story: [`concepts/openshell-config.md`](../concepts/openshell-config.md#audit-mode).

In a terminal: `brig help audit-mode`.

### Audit trail<a id="audit-trail"></a>

brig's own history of each VM: every request allowed or denied, policy revisions and who made them, drafts, sandboxes and brig commands.

Also called: history, audit log, collector, journal, retention, prune.

See also: [Verdict](#verdict), [Drafted rule](#draft), [Sandbox policy](#policies), [Activity](#activity).

```sh
brig audit dev webapp --since 7d
brig audit dev webapp --summary
brig audit status
```

In `brig ui`: `/host`.

The whole story: [`concepts/audit-trail.md`](../concepts/audit-trail.md).

In a terminal: `brig help audit-trail`.

### Base image<a id="base-image"></a>

A read-only image of Fedora with OpenShell, built on this host without root. VMs boot from an overlay of it.

Also called: mkosi, upgrade.

See also: [Root disk](#root-disk), [Data disk](#data-disk), [Sandbox image](#sandbox-image).

```sh
brig image build
brig upgrade dev
```

In `brig ui`: `/images`.

The whole story: [`concepts/disks-and-images.md`](../concepts/disks-and-images.md#base-images).

In a terminal: `brig help base-image`.

### Base policy<a id="base-policy"></a>

The policy the sandbox was created with, plus the rules added to it since, such as with Allow….

See also: [Effective policy](#effective-policy), [Policy file](#policy-file).

```sh
openshell policy get webapp --base
brig policy diff dev webapp
```

The whole story: [`concepts/openshell-config.md`](../concepts/openshell-config.md#base-and-effective-policy).

In a terminal: `brig help base-policy`.

### Config directory<a id="config-dir"></a>

A directory on this host with provider profiles, providers and policies, which sync applies to a VM's gateway.

Also called: openshell config, providers/, profiles/.

See also: [Sync](#config-sync), [Provider](#provider), [Policy file](#policy-file).

```sh
brig update dev --add-openshell-config ~/src/agent-openshell
```

The whole story: [`concepts/openshell-config.md`](../concepts/openshell-config.md#config-directories).

In a terminal: `brig help config-dir`.

### Data disk<a id="data-disk"></a>

The VM's disk at /home/agent: gateway state, secrets, images and sandbox workspaces. Kept on upgrade, deleted with the VM.

See also: [Root disk](#root-disk), [Base image](#base-image).

The whole story: [`concepts/disks-and-images.md`](../concepts/disks-and-images.md#disks).

In a terminal: `brig help data-disk`.

### Drafted rule<a id="draft"></a>

A rule OpenShell drafts from a sandbox's denied requests. Approve it to add it to that sandbox, or reject it.

Also called: drafts, approve, reject.

See also: [Fence 1, the sandbox policy](#fence-1), [Policy file](#policy-file).

```sh
brig policy allow dev webapp HOST --draft ID
```

The whole story: [`how-to/unblock.md`](../how-to/unblock.md#allow-it-for-this-sandbox).

In a terminal: `brig help draft`.

### Effective policy<a id="effective-policy"></a>

What the sandbox enforces right now: its base policy plus the rules of its attached providers.

See also: [Base policy](#base-policy), [Provider](#provider).

```sh
openshell policy get webapp --full
```

The whole story: [`concepts/openshell-config.md`](../concepts/openshell-config.md#base-and-effective-policy).

In a terminal: `brig help effective-policy`.

### Fence 1, the sandbox policy<a id="fence-1"></a>

Each sandbox's policy decides, per host, program, method and path, what may leave. Changes reload at once.

Also called: fence 1, proxy, egress.

See also: [Fence 2, the network profile](#fence-2), [Verdict](#verdict), [Drafted rule](#draft), [Sandbox policy](#policies).

```sh
brig policy allow dev webapp registry.npmjs.org --binary /usr/bin/node
```

In `brig ui`: `/traffic`.

The whole story: [`concepts/architecture.md`](../concepts/architecture.md#the-two-fences).

In a terminal: `brig help fence-1`.

### Fence 2, the network profile<a id="fence-2"></a>

The VM's network profile, enforced by nftables on the host, outside the VM. Root in the VM cannot lift it.

Also called: fence 2, network profile, nftables, lan, internet.

See also: [Fence 1, the sandbox policy](#fence-1), [VM](#vm).

```sh
brig update dev --profile default
brig show dev
```

The whole story: [`concepts/architecture.md`](../concepts/architecture.md#network-profiles-in-detail).

In a terminal: `brig help fence-2`.

### Gateway<a id="gateway"></a>

The OpenShell control plane inside a VM. Your host's openshell CLI reaches it as brig-NAME.

Also called: brig-NAME, openshell gateway, control plane.

See also: [VM](#vm), [Workspace](#workspace), [Using a VM from a terminal](#brig-use).

```sh
brig use dev
openshell sandbox list
```

In `brig ui`: `/gateway`.

The whole story: [`concepts/architecture.md`](../concepts/architecture.md#vm).

In a terminal: `brig help gateway`.

### Host directory<a id="mount"></a>

A directory on this host shared into a VM with virtiofs, read-only unless rw. A change applies to a running VM at once.

Also called: mount, virtiofs, share.

See also: [Sandbox volume](#sandbox-volume).

```sh
brig update dev --add-mount ~/src/kit:/srv/kit:ro
```

The whole story: [`how-to/share-directories.md`](../how-to/share-directories.md#into-the-vm).

In a terminal: `brig help mount`.

### Needs you<a id="needs-you"></a>

What blocks an agent or will bite later: failed syncs, host checks, older images, denied requests. Each item has its fix next to it.

See also: [Sync](#config-sync), [Fence 1, the sandbox policy](#fence-1).

```sh
brig up dev
```

In `brig ui`: `/`.

The whole story: [`how-to/web-ui.md`](../how-to/web-ui.md#what-it-shows).

In a terminal: `brig help needs-you`.

### Placeholder<a id="placeholder"></a>

What the agent sees instead of a secret, such as openshell:resolve:env:GH\_TOKEN.

Also called: openshell:resolve, credential_endpoint_mismatch.

See also: [Provider](#provider), [Provider profile](#provider-profile).

The whole story: [`concepts/openshell-config.md`](../concepts/openshell-config.md#placeholders).

In a terminal: `brig help placeholder`.

### Policy file<a id="policy-file"></a>

A policy in your config directory, such as policies/webapp.yaml, that new sandboxes are created from.

Also called: policy save, policies/.

See also: [Base policy](#base-policy), [Config directory](#config-dir).

```sh
brig policy save dev webapp --dry-run
brig policy save dev webapp
```

The whole story: [`how-to/unblock.md`](../how-to/unblock.md#keep-it-for-new-sandboxes).

In a terminal: `brig help policy-file`.

### Provider<a id="provider"></a>

A named credential on a gateway, such as a token. The agent sees a placeholder; the proxy adds the real value, only for the profile's endpoints.

Also called: credential, token, secret, api key.

See also: [Provider profile](#provider-profile), [Placeholder](#placeholder), [Sync](#config-sync), [Config directory](#config-dir).

```sh
brig sandbox attach dev webapp github
brig secret set dev github
brig sync dev
```

In `brig ui`: `/gateway?tab=providers`.

The whole story: [`concepts/openshell-config.md`](../concepts/openshell-config.md#providers-and-sandboxes).

In a terminal: `brig help provider`.

### Provider profile<a id="provider-profile"></a>

A kind of provider: which env vars hold the credential, how it is sent, to which endpoints and from which binaries.

Also called: profile, endpoints, binaries.

See also: [Provider](#provider), [Effective policy](#effective-policy).

```sh
openshell profile list
```

In `brig ui`: `/gateway?tab=profiles`.

The whole story: [`concepts/openshell-config.md`](../concepts/openshell-config.md#objects-on-a-gateway).

In a terminal: `brig help provider-profile`.

### Root disk<a id="root-disk"></a>

A throwaway overlay of the base image. Upgrade replaces it; nothing on it is meant to last.

See also: [Data disk](#data-disk), [Base image](#base-image).

The whole story: [`concepts/disks-and-images.md`](../concepts/disks-and-images.md#disks).

In a terminal: `brig help root-disk`.

### Sandbox<a id="sandboxes"></a>

A container on a gateway where an agent runs, fenced by its policy. Its directory /sandbox survives stop and start.

Also called: container, agent.

See also: [Sandbox policy](#policies), [Provider](#provider), [Sandbox template](#template), [Fence 1, the sandbox policy](#fence-1).

```sh
brig sandbox create dev --connect
brig sandbox connect dev webapp
```

In `brig ui`: `/sandboxes`.

The whole story: [`concepts/architecture.md`](../concepts/architecture.md#sandbox).

In a terminal: `brig help sandboxes`.

### Sandbox image<a id="sandbox-image"></a>

The container image a sandbox runs, kept in the VM's Podman. It is separate from the VM's base image.

Also called: container image, podman.

See also: [Sandbox template](#template), [Base image](#base-image).

```sh
brig image push dev localhost/pi-agent:latest
brig agent build dev claude
```

The whole story: [`concepts/disks-and-images.md`](../concepts/disks-and-images.md#sandbox-images).

In a terminal: `brig help sandbox-image`.

### Sandbox policy<a id="policies"></a>

Filesystem, process and network rules for one sandbox. OpenShell picks it when the sandbox is created.

Also called: global policy, default policy, OPENSHELL_SANDBOX_POLICY.

See also: [Base policy](#base-policy), [Effective policy](#effective-policy), [Policy file](#policy-file), [Fence 1, the sandbox policy](#fence-1).

```sh
openshell policy get webapp
```

In `brig ui`: `/gateway?tab=policies`.

The whole story: [`concepts/openshell-config.md`](../concepts/openshell-config.md#which-policy-a-sandbox-gets).

In a terminal: `brig help policies`.

### Sandbox template<a id="template"></a>

A named image and resources on a gateway that new sandboxes can start from.

Also called: templates.

See also: [Sandbox image](#sandbox-image), [Sandbox](#sandboxes).

```sh
openshell sandbox template list
```

In `brig ui`: `/gateway?tab=templates`.

The whole story: [`how-to/agents.md`](../how-to/agents.md#start-it).

In a terminal: `brig help template`.

### Sandbox volume<a id="sandbox-volume"></a>

A host directory offered to sandboxes as a read-only Podman volume, named after its tag, such as brig0.

Also called: volume.

See also: [Host directory](#mount), [Sandbox](#sandboxes).

```sh
brig sandbox create dev --mount ~/src/kit:/usr/local/share/kit -- --name kit
```

The whole story: [`how-to/share-directories.md`](../how-to/share-directories.md#into-a-sandbox).

In a terminal: `brig help sandbox-volume`.

### Sync<a id="config-sync"></a>

Applies a VM's config directories to its gateway: profiles, providers with secrets from your keyring, and the default policy.

Also called: brig sync, dry run, prune.

See also: [Config directory](#config-dir), [Provider](#provider).

```sh
brig sync dev --dry-run
brig sync dev
```

The whole story: [`concepts/openshell-config.md`](../concepts/openshell-config.md#what-a-sync-does).

In a terminal: `brig help config-sync`.

### Using a VM from a terminal<a id="brig-use"></a>

brig use NAME points the openshell CLI of the current shell at a VM's gateway, and at its default sandbox policy.

Also called: brig use, OPENSHELL_GATEWAY, shell.

See also: [Gateway](#gateway), [Workspace](#workspace).

```sh
brig use dev
brig use
brig use --unset
```

The whole story: [`start/install.md`](../start/install.md#shell-integration).

In a terminal: `brig help brig-use`.

### Verdict<a id="verdict"></a>

ALLOW means a rule let the request through. DENY means none did, and the request failed.

Also called: allow, deny, policy_denied.

See also: [Fence 1, the sandbox policy](#fence-1), [Audit mode](#audit-mode), [Drafted rule](#draft), [Audit trail](#audit-trail).

In `brig ui`: `/traffic`.

The whole story: [`how-to/unblock.md`](../how-to/unblock.md#see-what-was-denied).

In a terminal: `brig help verdict`.

### VM<a id="vm"></a>

A Fedora VM on this host that runs one OpenShell gateway and the sandboxes on it.

Also called: virtual machine, domain.

See also: [Gateway](#gateway), [Data disk](#data-disk), [Base image](#base-image), [Fence 2, the network profile](#fence-2).

```sh
brig list
brig show dev
brig up dev
```

In `brig ui`: `/vms`.

The whole story: [`concepts/architecture.md`](../concepts/architecture.md#vm).

In a terminal: `brig help vm`.

### Workspace<a id="workspace"></a>

A tenant inside a gateway, with its own sandboxes, providers and profiles. Most setups only have default.

Also called: tenant, -w.

See also: [Gateway](#gateway), [Sandbox](#sandboxes).

```sh
brig use dev -w team
brig sandbox list dev
```

The whole story: [`concepts/workspaces.md`](../concepts/workspaces.md).

In a terminal: `brig help workspace`.
